old.name: Château-Chalon vineyard walk
old.label: VINEYARD
old.hook: 2 h · the hilltop village + the AOC parcels
old.text: 2 h · the hilltop village + the AOC parcels Park at Château-Chalon village (15 km east of Lons), perched on a karst cliff. Walk up to the belvedere for the view east over the Bresse plain. Then descend through the Vin Jaune parcels of the Macle, Berthet-Bondet and Berthet-Bondet domaines on the blue-marl slope. Under 20 km of slope link Arbois, Pupillin and Château-Chalon — but the Château-Chalon AOC is the most concentrated 50 ha in France.

old.name: Savagnin — the genealogical centre of European white wine
old.label: WINE
old.hook: Parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner · = Traminer blanc
old.text: Parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner · = Traminer blanc EUR 18-45 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner Vinified two ways. Ouillé (topped-up): fresh, mineral, like a southern Burgundian Chardonnay but with more salt. Sous voile : oxidative, walnut and curry. DNA work (UC Davis / INRA, 1999) confirmed Savagnin = Traminer blanc, and that it is the parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner and Verdelho, and grandparent of Cabernet Sauvignon (via Sauvignon × Cabernet Franc). Gewürztraminer is its musqué mutation. The most genealogically central grape in European viticulture, planted on 0.0001 of European vineyard area. Where everywhere in the Jura

old.label: MUSEUM
old.hook: The world's most recognised processed-cheese brand was born here
old.text: The world's most recognised processed-cheese brand was born here EUR 8-12 WALK-IN All day One of the most internationally recognised food brands in the world was invented in Lons-le-Saunier (population 17,000) by Léon Bel in 1921. The painter Benjamin Rabier drew the laughing red cow in 1923 — a logo refined but never essentially changed since. The museum traces the brand's century of design, advertising, and global distribution. The cheese itself is technically a fromage fondu, distantly related to Comté processed-cheese byproducts. Where Lons — central

old.text: Ledoux's semicircular ideal-city, brine from 21.25 km away by saumoduc EUR 13-15 WALK-IN All day Claude-Nicolas Ledoux (1736–1806) designed the saltworks as a semicircular ideal-city around the Director's House at the focal point — a fusion of Enlightenment rationalism and industrial function. Construction 1775, operations 1779–1895. UNESCO 1982; the Salines de Salins-les-Bains (source of the brine) added to the listing 29 June 2009. The 21.25-km saumoduc — wooden pipeline replaced with cast iron from 1782 — carried concentrated brine through the Chaux forest, where firewood for evaporation was abundant. June–October Festival des Jardins. Where Arc-et-Senans — 25 km east

old.name: "Pasteur defended his thesis on Vin Jaune"
old.label: AVOID
old.hook: Honest correction — the 1857 paper was on lactic fermentation
old.text: Honest correction — the 1857 paper was on lactic fermentation A widely repeated story says Pasteur defended his doctoral thesis on the fermentation of Pupillin's Vin Jaune. The reality: his doctorate (1847) was on crystallography (tartaric-acid optical asymmetry). The 1857 work was a Mémoire sur la fermentation appelée lactique , read at the Académie des Sciences on 30 November 1857 — establishing that lactic fermentation is the work of living microorganisms. The Arbois work on wine spoilage that gave us pasteurisation came later. The myth blurs the timeline; the actual achievement is no less. Microbiology genuinely began at the foot of Jura barrels — just not as a doctoral thesis.

old_record.name: Maison de Louis Pasteur
tags: Maison des Illustres (2013) — Pasteur's home laboratory, preserved intact
old_record.why: Maison des Illustres (2013) — Pasteur's home laboratory, preserved intact. To order: the 1-hour guided visit; the experimental vineyard in Pupillin (Clos Pasteur) is still maintained. Family moved here 1827, when Pasteur was four. His 1857 Mémoire on lactic fermentation (Académie des Sciences, 30 November) was the foundational fermentation paper — not a doctoral thesis (his doctorate, 1847, was on crystallography). The Arbois lab is among the best-preserved 19th-c. scientific workplaces in France. One hour.
